name: list_devices
description: List all smart-home devices known to HOMEd. Each entry has the device `name`, an optional user `note` (free-text annotation set in homed-web UI — often hints at location, purpose or other context; omitted when empty) and a `properties` map keyed by endpoint ("common" or a numeric id). Individual sub-properties may carry a `display_name` — user-defined human-readable name set in homed-web UI; for multi-channel devices the device `name` is often generic (e.g. "Реле освещения") and the channel name (e.g. "Мастерская") lives inside the relevant sub-property's `display_name`. To find a device by a human phrase, call this with no filters and scan the device `name`, its `note` and the `display_name`s of its sub-properties — the full list is small enough.

service.description: Optional filter by HOMEd service topic (e.g. 'zigbee').

outputSchema.description: Matching devices (filtered by service/type when provided). Each item has the same shape as the get_device result.

available.description: Whether the device is currently online.

note.description: User-defined free-text annotation; omitted when empty.

properties.description: Endpoint key ("common" or numeric id) → map of sub-key → value/schema.

name: get_device
description: Return full information about a single device: its `name`, optional user `note` (free-text annotation, omitted when empty) and writable/readable properties with their current values and schema. Pass either the canonical key ("<type>/<id>") or the device name.

outputSchema.description: Full device info. `properties` is keyed by endpoint ("common" or a numeric id); each sub-property carries its current value plus schema (writable, enum/min/max/unit, display_name, history, note).

available.description: Whether the device is currently online.

note.description: User-defined free-text annotation; omitted when empty.

properties.description: Endpoint key ("common" or numeric id) → map of sub-key → value/schema.

name: set_properties
description:
Publish property updates to HOMEd devices in a single batch call. Always prefer one call with many operations to many sequential calls.

One operation targets ONE (device, endpoint) pair. To know what you can write, call get_device (or list_devices) and inspect `properties.<endpoint>`: every entry with `writable: true` may be set, the key is the exact sub-key you put under `properties`, and `enum`/`min`/`max`/`unit`/`note` describe the accepted value. For `endpoint`, echo the key exactly as it appears under `properties` in get_device: the string "common" or the numeric id (e.g. 5). `endpoint` may be omitted, which is treated the same as "common" (also use "common"/omit when sub-keys carry a `_N` suffix). Group several sub-keys of the same (device, endpoint) into one operation.

Operations are processed independently — failure on one does not abort the others.

operations.description: Array of independent updates. Each item targets ONE (device, endpoint) pair and may carry multiple sub-keys.

endpoint.description: The endpoint key exactly as it appears under `properties` in get_device: the string "common" or a numeric id (accepted as integer or string). Optional — omitting it is treated as "common". Set the numeric id when the sub-keys live under properties["<N>"]; use "common" (or omit) when they live in properties.common.

properties.description: Map of sub-key → target value, all written to the same td/ topic in ONE message. Keys are bare (e.g. "status", "level") when `endpoint` is a numeric id OR the device is single-endpoint; they carry a _N suffix (e.g. "status_5") only when the matching item is in common with a _N suffix and `endpoint` is "common"/omitted. Values: boolean for toggle/button, string for status/select/systemMode/etc., number for level/position/targetTemperature, array [r,g,b] for color.

outputSchema.description: One result per operation, in input order. Operations are independent — a failure on one does not affect the others.

device.description: Resolved device key, or the raw argument when the device was not found.

endpoint.description: The endpoint the operation targeted: "common" or the numeric id, echoed from the request.

topic.description: The td/ topic the payload was published to (present on success).

properties.description: Sub-keys written in this operation (present on success).

ok.description: Whether the operation was published successfully.

error.description: Failure reason (present when ok is false).

name: query_history
description: Query recorded values for a (device, endpoint, property) triple from homed-recorder. Only properties that carry `history: true` in get_device/list_devices are recorded — querying any other property returns an error. The response holds parallel arrays: `timestamp` (Unix timestamps in MILLISECONDS) plus `value` for raw samples, or — for long ranges — `timestamp` with hourly `avg`/`min`/`max` aggregates instead of `value`.

endpoint.description: The endpoint key exactly as it appears under `properties` in get_device: the string "common" or a numeric id (accepted as integer or string). Optional — omitting it is treated as "common". Set the numeric id when the property lives under properties["<N>"]; use "common" (or omit) when it lives in properties.common.

property.description: Property sub-key, exactly as it appears under properties.<endpoint> in get_device (must have `history: true`).

start.description: Range start, Unix timestamp in MILLISECONDS. Work out the plain Unix time in seconds for the calendar date/time you want, then multiply by 1000 (e.g. 2026-06-22 00:00 UTC = 1782086400 s = 1782086400000).

end.description: Range end, Unix timestamp in MILLISECONDS (Unix seconds × 1000). Pass 0 for "up to now".

outputSchema.description: Parallel arrays. `timestamp` is always present (Unix ms). For raw samples `value` is present; for aggregated long ranges `avg`/`min`/`max` are present instead of `value`.

timestamp.description: Sample times, Unix timestamps in MILLISECONDS.

value.description: Raw recorded values, aligned with `timestamp` (present for short ranges). Values are returned as strings (they are stored as text); an entry is null only when the device was unavailable at that sample.

avg.description: Hourly average, aligned with `timestamp` (present for long ranges).

min.description: Hourly minimum, aligned with `timestamp` (present for long ranges).

max.description: Hourly maximum, aligned with `timestamp` (present for long ranges).
